Payslip Deduction Items

Payslip deduction items are used to define various types of deductions that can be applied to employee payslips. These represent amounts withheld from employees' gross pay.

Common examples include income tax, social security contributions, health insurance premiums, retirement fund contributions, and loan repayments.

Setting Up Deduction Items

To create a new deduction item, click the New Payslip Item button. Each deduction item requires a name and can be linked to an account for proper accounting.

Once created, deduction items can be selected when preparing individual payslips. The same deduction item can be used across multiple employees and pay periods.

Managing Your Deductions

This list shows all deduction items available in your business. You can edit existing items or create new ones as your payroll requirements change.

Deduction items can be made inactive when no longer needed. Inactive items won't appear in selection lists but remain available for historical records.

Name
Name

The descriptive name identifying this deduction item. This name will appear on employee payslips and in payroll reports.

Choose names that clearly indicate the purpose of the deduction, such as Federal Income Tax, State Income Tax, Health Insurance Premium, 401(k) Contribution, or Student Loan Repayment.

Using standardized, consistent naming helps with payroll reporting and ensures employees easily understand their deductions.

Account
Account

The account where deducted amounts will be posted. This determines how the deduction is recorded in your accounting system.

Typically, deductions are posted to liability accounts (for amounts owed to third parties like tax authorities) or expense accounts (for employer-paid benefits).

If no account is selected, deductions will be posted to the Suspense account, which should be cleared by allocating to proper accounts.

Reporting Category
Reporting Category

Optional reporting category used to group similar deduction items for analysis and reporting purposes.

Categories help organize deductions into meaningful groups like Tax Deductions, Insurance Deductions, or Retirement Contributions for clearer payroll reports.
